text:
maria: Heads-up — after the kernel-selection change yesterday we're seeing a 25-35% regression on long-chat workloads when running on SM90 machines with CUDA 12.2. Short seqs are fine, it's the long tails (seq_len 2048+) that spike. nvprof/NSYS traces attached below.

aj: ugh. did we change the paged-attn selector threshold?

maria: yes — selector now prefers the new fused-paged kernel for cases where median(seq_len) > 512. That was intended to improve tail latency, but on SM90 it ends up invoking a Triton fallback path that is much slower for our batching mix.

li: can you paste the perf numbers?

maria: quick numbers from the microbench:
- SM80 (cuda 12.1) fused-paged: p50=22ms, tokens/s=1100
- SM90 (cuda 12.2) fused-paged -> triton fallback: p50=30ms, tokens/s=800
- SM90 forced cuda kernel (older selector): p50=18ms, tokens/s=1300

maria: NSYS snippet below (trimmed):
```
GPU activities: 76% stall due to synchronization
Kernel launches: fused_paged_triton_wrapper  -> lots of small kernels
Memcopy: increased host<->device traffic around KV page refill
```

sandeep: interesting, memcopy spikes suggest KV page churn. Are we spilling KV to host more on SM90 because of different L2/DRAM balancing?

maria: looks like it. The paging heuristic uses available GPU free memory and a target page size. On SM90 the runtime reports slightly different free memory due to driver allocator behaviour, so we pick a smaller page size which increases refill frequency.

aj: that combination (smaller pages + triton fallback) explains the perf cliff. Fused-paged expected to amortize kernel overhead across larger pages; small pages defeat that and then fallback pays the cost.

li: two quick experiments to triage: 1) force old CUDA fused kernel on an SM90 box (FORCE_KERNEL=fused_cuda) 2) simulate larger page size via env override (KV_PAGE_BYTES=64MB) and compare.

maria: already ran both. Results: forcing fused_cuda recovers p50 and throughput (matches SM80 numbers). Increasing KV_PAGE_BYTES helps ~15% but still worse than forcing fused_cuda. So fallback overhead dominates.

perf-bot: deploy check: rollout 2026-04-12/selector-v2 applied to 3 clusters (sm90-prod included). Canary pass flagged.

aj: recollection: Triton build we ship lacks a specific kernel fusion for SM90 tensor core warp shapes (compute capability differences). Triton ends up launching many small kernels instead of a single fused one. We probably need a Triton patch or prefer cuda path on SM90 until patch lands.

sandeep: can we short-circuit selector: prefer cuda kernel if device >= sm90 and cuda_version >= 12.2? Or better: detect if fused_cuda available for model shape/seq and prefer it.

maria: drafted a hotfix on selector to add an architecture-aware override:
```
if device_arch >= 90 and fused_cuda_available:
    prefer = fused_cuda
elif fallback_is_triton and expected_page_refills > threshold:
    prefer = fused_cuda
```
Applied to canary cluster for immediate mitigation.

li: we should also add a perf test matrix to CI: run both kernels across SM80/SM90 with seq_len buckets [128,512,1024,2048] and the actual batching distribution. Right now CI covers only median payloads so this slipped by.

aj: agreed. I'll add a nightly microbench job that uploads NSYS flamegraphs to the perf artifacts bucket. Also add a check that flags when fallback increases host->device memcpy time by >10%.

maria: follow-ups:
- rollback selector-v2 on sm90-prod if canary doesn't stabilize (monitoring alert created)
- triage Triton kernel generation for SM90 (assign to eng-ml)
- add KV_PAGE_BYTES override docs and expose in console as an advanced knob

sandeep: sounds good. for immediate ops: can we set KV_PAGE_BYTES=64MB via config for affected customers?

maria: yes we can flip that per-cluster; doing it on two clusters now.

perf-bot: alert created: perf-regression sm90-prod - latency increase detected, alert_id=PR-2026-0412-03

aj: one more note — batching heuristic: selector currently uses median(seq_len) and total_tokens to pick batch splits. For multimodal/assistant workloads with wide seq variance median misleads. We should consider 90th percentile or histogram-aware split.

li: agree. I'll prototype a histogram-based selector that computes expected refills and kernel invocation counts; objective is minimize (invocations * kernel_overhead + data_transfer_cost).

maria: thanks all. TL;DR: regression caused by selector preferring fused-paged which triggers Triton fallback on SM90 due to kernel generation mismatch + smaller KV pages causing more refills. Hotfix applied to prefer fused_cuda on SM90 when available; longer-term fixes: Triton kernel patch + selector improvements + CI perf matrix. :thumbsup:

aj: thanks — keep the thread updated with rollback or perf numbers from canary.

li: will post NSYS links and CI job PR later today.
